adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two *different* email class hierarchies being instantiated in `sendAddGuestsEmails`: organizer emails via `new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ calEvent, teamMember })` and attendee emails via `new AttendeeScheduledEmail(calendarEvent, attendee)` / `new AttendeeAddGuestsEmail(calendarEvent, attendee)`. The finding asserts this mix is inherently incompatible and will cause TS/destructuring crashes, but the diff does not show the constructor signatures of `OrganizerScheduledEmail`/`OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` or `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to prove a mismatch. It is plausible that organizer templates use an options-object constructor while attendee templates use positional args, and nothing in the diff verifies a compile failure or runtime crash.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using an `EventManager` instantiated from `ctx.user` and credentials fetched with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. When the caller is a team admin/owner or an attendee (allowed by the permission checks) and not `booking.userId`, this uses the *caller’s* external calendar credentials rather than the organizer/booking owner’s credentials. adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB update correctly filters to `uniqueGuests` (excluding already-attending and blacklisted emails), but the email notification call uses the raw `guests` input: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, it sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` when `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. Therefore, if a caller resubmits an email that is already an attendee, that attendee will incorrectly receive the full scheduled/confirmation email instead of the “Guests Added” notification. This mismatch is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` call is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and then continues returning success (`return { message: "Guests added" }`). This means email-send failures are not surfaced to the client (the UI’s `onSuccess` toast will still fire because the mutation resolves successfully) and the actual error object isn’t logged (no `err` details). However, the core operation (adding attendees + updating calendar attendees) still succeeds, so this is more of an observability/UX concern than a verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests exist for any of the new behavior: addGuests.handler.ts, AddGuestsDialog.tsx, MultiEmail.tsx, and both email templates all have zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior across UI (BookingListItem.tsx wiring, new AddGuestsDialog.tsx, new MultiEmail.tsx), server (new addGuests TRPC route/handler/schema), and email sending (sendAddGuestsEmails plus new templates/files). The diff does not add or modify any test files alongside these changes, so the concern that the new behavior is untested is diff-grounded. However, the claim of "zero coverage" cannot be strictly verified from the diff alone (there could be existing tests elsewhere), but "no tests added for these new paths" is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The addGuests handler never checks booking.status, allowing guests to be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings and sending CONFIRMED ics invites for events that no longer exist

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`), the booking is fetched and updated without any check of `booking.status` (or equivalent) before allowing `attendees.createMany`. The email/ICS generation in the new templates (`packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts`) hardcodes `status: "CONFIRMED"` in `generateIcsString(...)`. If a booking can be CANCELLED/REJECTED, this diff would still allow adding guests and would send CONFIRMED invites/emails for a non-active booking, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 in addGuests.handler.ts:59-68 throws a raw Prisma NotFoundError instead of a TRPCError when booking.userId is null, causing an unstructured 500 error

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined`, this queries `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw Prisma's not-found error (not a `TRPCError`). There is no surrounding try/catch converting it to a `TRPCError`, so the mutation can fail with an internal/unstructured server error instead of a controlled TRPC error when `booking.userId` is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw guests array (including filtered-out emails) is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees redundantly included in the request to receive a full re-send of the original booking-confirmation email instead of the guests-added notice

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out already-present attendees and blacklisted emails, and only creates new attendee rows from `uniqueGuests`. However it calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original `guests` array (which may include existing attendee emails). In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, attendees whose email is in `newGuests` receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (full scheduled/confirmation email), otherwise they receive `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Passing the unfiltered `guests` therefore causes existing attendees that were redundantly included in the request to be treated as “new” and receive an unnecessary re-send of the scheduled email instead of the guests-added notice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built from the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's, so when a non-organizer attendee adds guests, the organizer's calendar event is never updated; the call is also outside try/catch after the DB commit, so a throw leaves committed rows with a confusing error on retry

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed using credentials from the requesting user (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` then `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`). If a non-organizer attendee triggers `addGuests`, they likely lack the organizer’s calendar credentials, so `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` may fail to update the organizer’s calendar. This call is also not wrapped in try/catch and occurs after the DB update (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), so a thrown error can leave guests committed in DB while calendar/email side-effects fail; a retry then hits `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and throws `BAD_REQUEST` despite the previous attempt partially succeeding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'Additional Guests' menu entry in BookingListItem.tsx:193-200 is rendered unconditionally, showing the action to users (non-admin team members, past bookings) the server will reject with FORBIDDEN, with no client-side gating mirroring the server's permission matrix

adjudication.rationale: In `BookingListItem.tsx`, the new menu item `{ id: "add_members", ... }` is appended to `menuItems` unconditionally and only opens `AddGuestsDialog` (no checks in the component). The server-side mutation `addGuestsHandler` can return `FORBIDDEN` based on user/booking relationship (`!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`). So the UI can present an action that will predictably fail for some users, but this is primarily a UX/consistency issue rather than a correctness/security bug because the server still enforces authorization and the client handles errors via toast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:60-66 state reset only happens on the Cancel button's onClick — closing via ESC, backdrop click, or the dialog's close affordance bypasses it, leaving stale emails and error banners when the dialog is reopened

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, internal state (multiEmailValue initialized to [""], and isInvalidEmail) is only reset in two places: the Cancel button onClick (resets both and closes) and the mutation onSuccess (resets and closes). However, the Dialog is controlled via `open={isOpenDialog}` and `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` with no handler to reset state when the dialog is closed via ESC/backdrop/close affordance. Those close paths will set `isOpenDialog` to false but leave `multiEmailValue`/`isInvalidEmail` unchanged, so reopening the dialog can show stale emails and the error banner.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission gate in addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 uses && instead of ||, so team admins who are not the team owner are incorrectly denied permission to add guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. The subsequent permission check (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`) will therefore incorrectly deny access to a team admin who is not also the owner. This matches the finding that `&&` should be `||` (or equivalent logic) to allow either role.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking-status check in the handler allows guests to be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings, and the generated ICS is emitted with status CONFIRMED for non-existent events

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the booking is fetched (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`) and then updated to add attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`) with no check of booking state/time (no status/`cancelled`/`rejected`/`endTime`/`startTime` gating) before mutating and sending calendar/email updates. Additionally, the new email templates generate an ICS payload with `status: "CONFIRMED"` unconditionally (`generateIcsString({ ... status: "CONFIRMED" })` in both `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`), so if the booking is not an active event this will still emit a confirmed invite/update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails at addGuests.handler.ts:138 is passed the raw input instead of uniqueGuests, so existing attendees filtered from the DB write still receive the full AttendeeScheduledEmail re-confirmation

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler filters out existing/blacklisted emails into `uniqueGuests` and only persists those (`createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }`). However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input list, not `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts), attendee emails that are included in the `newGuests` array receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (re-confirmation) instead of the “guests added” notification. Therefore if the input `guests` contains emails that were already attendees (filtered out from the DB write), those existing attendees can still match `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` and receive the re-confirmation email, as the finding claims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema (addGuests.schema.ts:4-6) only validates email format; the duplicate-email uniqueness constraint exists only in the client dialog, so direct API calls can create duplicate attendee rows and send multiple copies of emails

adjudication.rationale: The server input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (addGuests.schema.ts) only enforces `z.string().email()` and does not enforce uniqueness. In the server handler, `uniqueGuests` only filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but does not dedupe duplicates within the `guests` array itself (`uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`). Therefore a direct API call with duplicate new emails (e.g. `["a@b.com","a@b.com"]`) will result in `createMany` inserting multiple attendee rows with the same email and `sendAddGuestsEmails` iterating over `calendarEvent.attendees`, potentially sending multiple emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager at addGuests.handler.ts:146-152 is constructed with the requester's credentials instead of the organizer's, causing errors or wrong-calendar mutations when an attendee adds guests to an organizer's event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user` is `ctx.user` (the requester) and `credentials` come from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. However, the booking organizer is separately loaded as `organizer` and the booking includes `user.credentials`, yet neither is used for the EventManager construction. Since the mutation allows non-organizers (`isAttendee` case) to add guests, an attendee-triggered call will attempt `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using the attendee’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, plausibly leading to wrong-calendar mutations or failures when the attendee lacks calendar access for the organizer’s event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New attendees are created with name: "" at addGuests.handler.ts:71-79, causing blank names in the ICS attendee entries, email headers, and downstream artifacts

adjudication.rationale: The diff does create new booking attendees with an empty name in `addGuests.handler.ts` via `guestsFullDetails` (name: ""), and later propagates `attendee.name` into the `CalendarEvent` attendees list (`attendeesList`). This can result in empty/blank display names in generated email headers (e.g., `to: `${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>`` in `attendee-add-guests-email.ts`) and potentially in ICS content depending on how `generateIcsString` uses attendee names. However, given the UI only collects emails (no names), an empty name may be an acceptable/expected limitation rather than a definite correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The handler copies seatsPerTimeSlot into evt but never checks remaining seat capacity before createMany, allowing guests to be added past seatsPerTimeSlot for seated event types

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the code unconditionally appends new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}})` without any check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` / existing attendee count. Yet it copies `seatsPerTimeSlot` into the emitted `evt` (`seatsPerTimeSlot: booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`), indicating seated-capacity is relevant. As written, a seated event can have additional attendees added past its seat limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tooltip content "Remove email" in MultiEmail.tsx:64 is hardcoded English while the rest of the file uses t() for localization

adjudication.rationale: In packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx, the Tooltip uses a hardcoded English string: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` while the component otherwise uses `useLocale()` and `t(...)` (e.g., `t("add_another")`). This is a diff-grounded i18n consistency issue (missing localization), not a functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmailLazy and its export in packages/ui/index.tsx add an untested, single-use component to the shared design-system package's public API surface with a misleading justification comment and buggy empty-value behavior (blank required field, silent no-op Add button)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new UI component (packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx) and a lazy wrapper (MultiEmailLazy.tsx) and then exports it from the shared design-system public entrypoint (packages/ui/index.tsx: `export { default as MultiEmail } ...`). In the shown changes it is only used by the new `AddGuestsDialog` in the web app, so this does expand the shared package’s public API surface for what appears (from this diff) to be a feature-specific need. However, the claimed “buggy empty-value behavior” is not clearly verified from the diff: MultiEmail’s add buttons do mutate state (push ""), and the dialog’s Add handler validates emails and shows an error rather than silently no-op’ing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization in addGuests.handler.ts:51-53 uses && instead of || when checking isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, rejecting team admins who are not owners with FORBIDDEN even though the permission model intends admin or owner

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. Given the variable name and the subsequent permission gate (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`), this will incorrectly forbid team admins who are not owners from adding guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist bypass via case sensitivity in addGuests.handler.ts:74-84: blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased but guest is compared as-is, so a case-variant email like 'Blocked@Example.com' bypasses the blacklist; the same un-normalized guest compared against existing attendees also allows duplicate attendee rows

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, blacklistedGuestEmails are normalized to lowercase (split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())), but the filter compares them against `guest` without normalizing (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so a case-variant address (e.g., "Blocked@Example.com") would not match and would bypass the blacklist. The same lack of normalization is used when checking existing attendees (`guest === attendee.email`), so case-variants can slip through and create duplicate attendee rows via `createMany` even if the same email already exists with different casing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema in addGuests.schema.ts has no uniqueness or size constraint on guests, so intra-request duplicates (e.g. ['a@x.com', 'a@x.com']) create duplicate attendee rows since uniqueGuests only filters against existing attendees and there is no DB unique constraint on (bookingId, email)
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate highlights that duplicates within the same request (e.g., repeated emails) are not deduplicated by uniqueGuests (it only filters against existing/blacklisted), which can lead createMany to insert duplicate attendee rows. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment, with extra notes about schema/DB constraints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails at addGuests.handler.ts:168-170 is passed the unfiltered guests input instead of uniqueGuests, so already-attendees and blacklisted guests still receive emails, including duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmails for existing attendees

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, guests are filtered into uniqueGuests for DB creation, but sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the original unfiltered input. sendAddGuestsEmails decides which template to send based on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` while iterating over `calendarEvent.attendees`. If the caller includes an email that is already an attendee, that existing attendee will match and incorrectly receive an AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of an “guests added” notification. (Blacklisted emails won’t receive emails because they aren’t in `calendarEvent.attendees`, but the unfiltered list still causes wrong email selection for existing attendees.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager at addGuests.handler.ts:160-166 is constructed from ctx.user (the requester) instead of the booking organizer, so updateCalendarAttendees uses the caller's credentials and the organizer's calendar event is not updated or the call fails, despite booking.user.credentials being explicitly included in the query

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation allows non-organizers to add guests (`isTeamAdminOrOwner || isOrganizer || isAttendee`), but the calendar update is performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user` is `ctx.user` (the requester) and `credentials` comes from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (lines ~160-166). Even though the booking query includes `booking.user.credentials`, those organizer credentials are never used. If the requester is an attendee/admin (not the organizer), `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run with the wrong identity/credentials, plausibly failing or updating the wrong calendar, so the organizer’s calendar may not be updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic multi-system write in addGuests.handler.ts:98-166: attendees are persisted to the DB, then eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs outside any try/catch, so a calendar update failure leaves committed attendee rows with no compensation while the client sees an error and retries into partial state

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the mutation first commits new attendees to the DB via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding try/catch and no transaction spanning both systems. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (calendar provider/API failure), the TRPC call will error while the DB write remains committed, leaving a partial state and making client retries likely to encounter inconsistent/duplicate behavior. This non-atomic multi-system write is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking state guard in addGuests.handler.ts:27-49: guests can be added to cancelled or past bookings, causing guests to receive a CONFIRMED ICS that re-creates a cancelled event on their calendar and emails attendees about a nonexistent booking

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking by `id` and proceeds to append attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), updates calendar attendees, and sends ICS/email (`sendAddGuestsEmails`) without any guard on booking lifecycle state (e.g., cancelled) or timing (e.g., `booking.startTime` in the past). The constructed `CalendarEvent` and both email templates generate an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"`, so if this mutation is invoked for a cancelled/past booking it can notify guests and potentially re-add/refresh the event on calendars. The diff shows no checks that prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: seatsPerTimeSlot capacity is never enforced in addGuests.handler.ts:89-115; nothing validates booking.attendees.length + uniqueGuests.length <= seatsPerTimeSlot, allowing seated event types to exceed capacity

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new guests are appended via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without any check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`. The handler even includes `seatsPerTimeSlot` on the constructed `CalendarEvent` (`evt.seatsPerTimeSlot = booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`) but never validates that `booking.attendees.length + uniqueGuests.length` stays within capacity. This allows adding guests to a seated event beyond its configured limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) at addGuests.handler.ts:63-71 leaks a raw Prisma P2025 error as a 500 for bookings with null userId instead of proper booking_not_found handling; same sentinel-integer pattern as teamId ?? 0 on line 51

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is null/undefined, this queries `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (Prisma P2025) without being converted to a TRPCError, resulting in a 500 rather than a controlled `booking_not_found`/validation error. This is a real correctness issue in the newly added handler. The similar `teamId ?? 0` sentinel usage further suggests these nullable IDs are expected in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failure in addGuests.handler.ts:168-172 is swallowed with console.log without the exception object and the handler still returns 'Guests added', so the organizer is never told attendees weren't notified

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the function still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This is diff-grounded: failures are swallowed (no rethrow) and the error isn’t logged with the exception object. However, the core operation (adding attendees + updating calendar attendees) has already succeeded, so returning success isn’t strictly incorrect; it’s more an important reliability/observability issue and could mislead users about notifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: newGuests.includes(attendee.email) in email-manager.ts:522-547 is case-sensitive, compounding the normalization issue: case-variant emails of existing attendees are classified as new, receive the full AttendeeScheduledEmail, and are created as duplicate rows; all membership checks should use a normalized key

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts), `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is a case-sensitive membership test. In the added handler `addGuests.handler.ts`, guest emails are compared against existing attendees using strict equality (`guest === attendee.email`) and are inserted as-is; there is no normalization (e.g., lowercasing/trim) on either side (only the blacklist is lowercased). This makes it possible for case-variant duplicates (e.g., `User@x.com` vs `user@x.com`) to be treated as “new” and inserted, and also misclassified in email sending (receiving the wrong template). Membership checks and storage should use a normalized key.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization check in addGuests.handler.ts uses && instead of || , collapsing 'team admin or owner' into 'team admin and owner', so plain team admins or owners who aren't both get FORBIDDEN on bookings they should manage

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`: `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass the later permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`, which will wrongly forbid users who are only admins or only owners. The variable name and typical intent (“admin or owner”) indicate this should be `||`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email step is passed raw `guests` instead of deduplicated, server-filtered `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees (including case-insensitive email matches that slip through) to receive a duplicate full 'AttendeeScheduledEmail' with fresh ICS invite instead of the correct 'new guests added' email

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server filters `guests` into `uniqueGuests` for DB insertion, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw, unfiltered input. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts), the logic `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (fresh ICS) to any attendee whose email is present in that `newGuests` array. Therefore, if the client submits an email that is already an attendee (allowed by the server schema, which does not enforce uniqueness vs existing attendees), that existing attendee will incorrectly receive a full scheduled/invite email instead of the intended "guests added" email. Additionally, the server-side filtering against existing attendees is case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`), so case-variant duplicates can slip through and exacerbate misclassification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist comparison is case-asymmetric: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but `guest` is not, so a blacklisted address like `Admin@Blocked.com` bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entirely

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` values are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates format (`z.string().email()`) and does not lowercase, a differently-cased email (e.g. `Admin@Blocked.com`) would not match the lowercase blacklist entry and would bypass the blacklist filter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update in addGuests.handler.ts is executed with the requesting user's credentials instead of the organizer's, so when an attendee adds guests the organizer's external calendar event is never updated (or the update errors after the DB write commits), leaving DB and calendar state divergent

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the external calendar update is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using an `EventManager` constructed from the requesting `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The organizer is fetched separately (`organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow(...)`) but their credentials are never used. This means if a non-organizer attendee invokes `addGuests`, the calendar update will run with the attendee’s credentials (likely lacking access to the organizer’s destination calendar / event references), so the calendar update can fail or no-op after the DB `booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` has already committed, creating DB vs external calendar divergence. The diff also shows no try/catch around `updateCalendarAttendees`, so any error would abort after DB mutation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Notification failures in the try/catch around sendAddGuestsEmails are swallowed with a bare console.log that doesn't even log `err`, so the UI shows success while added guests never receive their invite email and the failure is undiagnosable in production

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log `err` or propagate the failure. The handler then still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the client mutation `onSuccess` path shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")` even if email sending failed, and production diagnostics lose the underlying error details.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation-error state `isInvalidEmail` is never cleared on retry in AddGuestsDialog.tsx — setIsInvalidEmail(false) only fires on Cancel, so the 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner persists through a valid successful mutation until dialog unmount

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed client-side validation (`handleAdd` else-branch), but it is never reset on subsequent valid attempts or on successful mutation. `onSuccess` closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`, but does not call `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`, so the error banner can remain visible during a retry and can reappear when the dialog is reopened because the component stays mounted (it’s always rendered in BookingListItem and only controlled via `open`). It is only cleared in the Cancel button handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer email's replyTo includes newly added guests as plain email strings with no names (attendees created with name: "" and uniqueGuests.map drops names), so organizer's Reply All shows bare addresses and input-time names are silently lost

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the organizer email sets `replyTo` as an array of plain email strings: `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`, so newly added guests will appear without display names in Reply-To. Also, in `addGuests.handler.ts`, new guests are created with `name: ""`, so even if names were desired later, they are not captured/stored. However, the UI (`MultiEmail`) only collects emails (no names), so this is more a UX/feature limitation than a verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization predicate uses && instead of || so isTeamAdminOrOwner requires the user to be both admin and owner, breaking the intended authorization path

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`: `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Given the variable name and the later auth gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, this requires a user to be both team admin and team owner to pass via the team-role path. If the intended authorization is “admin OR owner”, then admins who aren’t owners (or owners who aren’t admins) will be incorrectly forbidden from adding guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The team admin check runs against teamId ?? 0 which is meaningless when booking.eventType is null for non-team bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed by calling `isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)` and `isTeamOwner(..., booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)`. If `booking.eventType` is `null`/`undefined`, those checks run against `teamId` 0, which is likely not a real team and makes the team-permission check ineffective/fragile (at minimum unnecessary queries; potentially problematic if those helpers assume a valid teamId). The diff doesn’t prove this causes incorrect authorization in practice because organizer/attendee checks still gate access, but the concern is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blacklist is bypassable via case-sensitivity because guest emails are not lowercased before comparison

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but incoming `guests` are compared as-is: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` is not lowercased (and `z.string().email()` does not enforce lowercase), a blacklisted email like `blocked@example.com` can bypass the check by submitting `Blocked@Example.com`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The guest === attendee.email strict comparison defeats the duplicate attendee check when existing attendee email was stored with different casing

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the duplicate-attendee prevention uses a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` when computing `uniqueGuests`. Since neither the input schema (`z.string().email()`) nor this code normalizes casing, an existing attendee stored as `Foo@bar.com` would not match an input `foo@bar.com`, allowing a duplicate attendee to be added and also affecting later logic like `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in `sendAddGuestsEmails` (also case-sensitive).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The zod schema at addGuests.schema.ts has no .refine for intra-request duplicate guests; dedupe only exists client-side in AddGuestsDialog.tsx

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not prevent intra-request duplicates. While the client dialog adds a `.refine` uniqueness check, the server handler `addGuestsHandler` also does not dedupe within `guests` (it filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but not duplicates in the submitted array) before `createMany`. This means a direct API call (or bypassing client validation) can create duplicate attendee rows for the same email in a single request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any booking attendee can add an unbounded number of guests (no .max() in schema, no rate limit, no per-booking attendee cap), enabling spam/DoS via mass email and calendar fan-out

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) and the handler creates attendees via `createMany` and triggers `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` plus `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (addGuests.handler.ts). Also, permission allows any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to call it. Nothing in the diff enforces a per-booking cap, per-request cap, or any rate limiting, so a caller can submit a very large array and cause mass DB writes + email/calendar fan-out (spam/DoS potential).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed with the requesting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials when mutating the organizer's external calendar event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code constructs `EventManager` using the requesting session user (`...user` from `ctx.user`) and credentials fetched via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. Since the handler allows non-organizers (e.g., an attendee via `isAttendee`) to add guests, this will attempt to mutate the booking's external calendar event using the requester's credentials rather than the booking organizer's credentials (`booking.userId` / `organizer`), which can cause incorrect/failed calendar updates and violates the intended ownership of the organizer's calendar integration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email sending error is swallowed with a bare console.log that discards the err object, losing the audit trail and observability for a state-changing operation

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email dispatch is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The catch both swallows the failure (no rethrow/monitoring) and discards the `err` object, reducing observability/auditability for a state-changing mutation (guests are already persisted and calendar updated). This is a diff-grounded reliability/monitoring concern rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: data-testid collision: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:94 button uses data-testid="add_members" which duplicates the dropdown item id "add_members" in BookingListItem.tsx:193, causing strict-mode violations or wrong element clicks in Playwright tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a dropdown/menu item with an object property `id: "add_members"` in `BookingListItem.tsx`, and a separate button in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` with `data-testid="add_members"`. However, the diff does not show the dropdown item rendering its `id` as a DOM `id` or `data-testid`, so an actual `data-testid` collision (and the claimed Playwright/strict-mode impact) cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleAdd empty-list guard in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:46-51 is dead code because multiEmailValue is initialized to [""] (length 1), so the guard never fires; users clicking Add on a fresh dialog get a misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error instead of a no-op

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, multiEmailValue is initialized to [""] (line ~27) and also reset to [""] on cancel/success. Therefore the `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) return;` guard in handleAdd can never trigger for a freshly opened dialog (length is 1). Clicking Add without typing an email runs `safeParse([""])`, which fails the `.email()` check and sets `isInvalidEmail` true, showing the generic `emails_must_be_unique_valid` message. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/validation defect (dead guard + misleading error path for empty input).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unit/integration tests for addGuests.handler.ts covering permission matrix, blacklisted-email filtering, and duplicate-attendee filtering

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new server-side logic in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts` (permission checks via `isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner`, filtering out existing attendees and `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, and rejecting when `uniqueGuests.length === 0`), but the PR diff shows no accompanying unit/integration tests added for this new handler path. While the repo might have existing coverage elsewhere, nothing in the shown diff adds tests for these behaviors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests for sendAddGuestsEmails branching logic distinguishing AttendeeScheduledEmail for new guests vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail for pre-existing attendees

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new branching behavior in `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts) that chooses `AttendeeScheduledEmail` when `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` and `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` otherwise. No test files or test additions are shown anywhere in the diff to cover this new conditional mapping behavior, so the review concern about missing tests for this specific branching logic is grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: try/catch at addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 swallows email-send errors with a bare console.log

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the code wraps `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` in a `try/catch` and, on error, only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without rethrowing or logging `err`. This does swallow email-send failures and provides poor diagnostics/observability, but it’s not clearly a functional defect since the mutation may intentionally succeed even if notifications fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guest rows are committed to the DB before the external calendar write with no transaction or compensating rollback, so if updateCalendarAttendees throws (expired OAuth token, provider outage, rate limit) the Attendee rows remain committed while the calendar is not updated and no notification email is sent; the uniqueGuests dedup filter then treats the guest as already added on retry, permanently skipping the calendar write with no remove-guests endpoint to undo it

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB is mutated first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}})` before calling the external side effect `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. There is no Prisma transaction wrapping both operations and no compensating rollback if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, so new attendee rows can remain committed while the external calendar is not updated. Additionally, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already present in `booking.attendees`, so a retry after a partial failure will likely yield `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and throw `BAD_REQUEST`, preventing the calendar update from ever being retried for those already-inserted guests. The email send is also skipped if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws because the `try/catch` only wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) at addGuests.handler.ts:170 is passed the raw unfiltered input instead of uniqueGuests, so existing attendees who were redundantly re-submitted match newGuests.includes() in email-manager.ts:536 and receive a duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail (a re-send of the original booking confirmation), causing written DB data and communicated email data to diverge
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core bug: sendAddGuestsEmails bases “new guest” detection on the input guests array (newGuests) while iterating over the full calendarEvent.attendees list, so re-submitted/existing attendees can satisfy newGuests.includes(attendee.email) and be treated as newly added (triggering the wrong/duplicate email type). The candidate adds detail about passing raw vs uniqueGuests, but it’s the same underlying mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The server schema addGuests.schema.ts:5-6 omits the uniqueness refinement that exists only on the client, so duplicate emails within a single request pass the uniqueGuests filter (which only deduplicates against existing attendees) and reach createMany, either creating duplicate Attendee rows with identical (bookingId, email) or throwing an unhandled Prisma P2002 error as a 500 instead of the intended unable_to_add_guests error path

adjudication.rationale: In the server input schema (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`) `guests` is only `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint, while the client dialog adds a uniqueness `refine`. In the handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`), `uniqueGuests` filters only against existing `booking.attendees` and the blacklist, but does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. As a result, a request like `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` can reach `attendees.createMany` with duplicates, which can either create duplicate attendee rows (if no DB unique constraint) or throw an uncaught Prisma error during `booking.update` (no try/catch around the DB write), yielding an unintended server error instead of a controlled validation error.
